title: DNA Extraction from Zooplankton in 96 Wells
author: coline.royaux

steps.title: Prepare extraction plate and label
steps.instruction: Set up a 96‑well extraction plate, placing one zooplankton individual in each well and alternating genus between wells to allow detection of cross‑contamination. Label the plate accordingly.

steps.title: Collect and record specimen
steps.instruction: Collect a single individual from the sample, note its genus, and determine its sex using a binocular microscope.

steps.title: Process specimens by size
steps.instruction: For individuals larger than 5 mm, dissect a few legs, place the legs in the well, and keep the remaining body in a tagged Eppendorf tube. For individuals smaller than 5 mm, place the whole body in the well. If needed, add alcohol to the well to let the material settle at the bottom.

steps.title: Dry specimens and seal plate
steps.instruction: Allow the biological material in all 96 wells to dry. If excess alcohol remains, remove it with a micropipette. Close the plate securely before any transport.

steps.title: Prepare lysis mixture
steps.instruction: In a multi‑channel reservoir, mix 18 mL T1 buffer with 2.5 mL K proteinase.

steps.title: Add lysis mixture to wells
steps.instruction: Using a multimicropipette, dispense the lysis reagents into each well.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 200 µL of the T1 + K proteinase mixture into each well.
Alternatively, add 180 µL T1 buffer and 25 µL K proteinase to each well.

steps.title: Seal plate with foil and film
steps.instruction: Close the extraction plate with heated aluminium foil and an adhesive plastic film.

steps.title: Incubate plate for lysis
steps.instruction: Place the sealed plate in a proofer set to 56 °C and incubate overnight (minimum 6 h) to lyse the tissues.

steps.title: Load plate into extraction robot
steps.instruction: Remove the adhesive film and aluminium foil, then load the plate into the DNA extraction robot.

steps.title: Add BQ1 buffer and ethanol
steps.instruction: The robot deposits 200 µL BQ1 buffer and 200 µL ethanol into each well and mixes the contents.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to binding plate
steps.instruction: Transfer 600 µL of each well’s content (lysate, BQ1, ethanol) onto the tissue‑binding plate; discard excess reagents into a waste container.

steps.title: Dry binding plate to bind DNA
steps.instruction: Dry the tissue‑binding plate by aspirating for 00:05:00 (5 min) to allow DNA to bind to the silica membrane.

steps.title: Wash silica membrane
steps.instruction: Perform sequential washes of the silica membrane:

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL BW buffer per well and aspirate dry for 00:05:00.
Add 900 µL B5 buffer per well, aspirate dry for 00:05:00; repeat a second wash with 900 µL B5 buffer and another 00:05:00 aspiration.

steps.title: Final dry before elution
steps.instruction: Remove the waste container, then dry the binding plate again by aspirating for 00:10:00 (10 min).

steps.title: Place empty extraction plate
steps.instruction: Position an empty 96‑well extraction plate beneath the binding plate to receive the eluate.

steps.title: First DNA elution
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL BE buffer to each well of the binding plate; the eluate collects in the underlying extraction plate.

steps.title: Rest and second elution
steps.instruction: After a 00:03:00 (3 min) rest, dry the binding plate for 00:02:00 (2 min) and repeat the elution with another 100 µL BE buffer per well.

steps.title: Retrieve DNA plate and discard waste
steps.instruction: Remove the extraction plate now containing the genomic DNA and discard the used binding plate and any remaining waste.
